title: Orchestration: deterministic context first, opt-in weak-model scout, measured delegation
decision:
1. Default context is deterministic: `plan.py start` builds the context pack from JSON (P2.2). No model call.
2. Scout is opt-in (`plan.settings.scout=auto` or `start --scout`): a weak model configured per provider in `packages/task/configs/command-routing.json` → `orchestration.scout.<provider>` (`model`, `effort`, `argv`, `timeout_s`) reads the pack and returns ≤ 40 lines of "path[:symbol] — why" plus unknowns into `context/<item>.scout.md`. It never writes code or decisions. Failure is non-fatal.
3. Orchestration inside an item is part of the schema (owner M3/M4): the item gets a workspace sub-folder `phases/<Pn>/<Pn.m>/` holding one `<U#>.json` per work unit and a `<U#>/` folder for the worker (generated `brief.md`, reports, logs); `item.units[]` lists the unit ids. A unit has owned `files`, `depends_on`, `checks`, minimum `route`, `mode` (`self|delegate|either`) and lifecycle `status` (`todo → dispatched → returned → accepted|reworked|rejected`). `plan.py unit … dispatch` writes the worker's `brief.md`; independent units (no dependency path, disjoint files — enforced by `check`) may run in parallel. The item executor is always the integrator: it reviews and tests every returned piece and alone finishes the item. Every transition is logged as a `delegate` event.
4. `plan.py stats` aggregates scout/delegate outcomes and friction per plan; turning scout or delegation on by default requires a later owner decision based on these numbers.
rationale:
- "Must not get worse" (B9): evidence supports a scout only as a router and shows over-fetching risks (R4); keeping the strong executor responsible for reading and verifying limits the downside.
- Deterministic packs already deliver most of the "prepared context" value without model cost or provider-CLI fragility.
- Measuring before defaulting follows the philosophy's "unmeasured idea → trigger" rule while still delivering the owner's prioritized capability.
consequences: P1.1 puts `units` into the item schema; P2.2 reserves pack section 13 for the scout map; P4.1 implements scout and config; P4.2 implements `plan.py unit`, unit mini-packs, the disjointness check and `stats`.
Provider CLIs for scout are verified at P4.1 execution (`--help`); a provider without a usable non-interactive CLI gets no scout entry.

evidence.note: RAG ✅ 2026-10-05 perplexity-web: scout as index/router; ContextBench 2026: scaffolding gives small retrieval gains, unused context, recall over precision; no measurement that cheap-briefing-first raises pass rate
